questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: When 18-year-olds were first allowed to vote in the UK
Whether and why people's politics change with age
How to choose a political party that matches your values
Why young people don't vote in general elections
questions.why: They ask whether we become more right-wing as we get older, and why.

questions.q: How does Sam feel her political views have changed?
options: They have completely changed since she was a student
She has lost all interest in politics and stopped voting
She's better informed but agrees with the same things
She now supports the opposite side from her parents
questions.why: She says her views are better informed but she still generally agrees with the same things.

questions.q: Why does Sam object when Neil says 'many, many, many years'?
options: She doesn't want to sound old
She has never voted
She thinks he is wrong about the date
She doesn't remember voting
questions.why: She says 'not so much with the manys' and approves of 'very, very few years'.

questions.q: According to Professor Tilley, what is one plausible reason older people change their views?
options: They earn more money
They watch more TV news
Their friends influence them
They become more resistant to change
questions.why: He says people 'become a bit more resistant to change as they get older'.

questions.q: What other change does Professor Tilley say happens with age?
options: People become more revolutionary
People become less idealistic
People stop voting
People become more emotional
questions.why: He says they also tend to become less idealistic.

questions.q: Why might right-wing parties attract older people?
options: Their platforms tend to support keeping things the same
They promise big changes to pensions and the economy
They usually have younger and more exciting leaders
They spend much more on education and universities
questions.why: He says parties on the right may be more favourable to the status quo.

questions.q: According to Professor Tilley, older people's politics are more about what?
options: Idealism
Revolution
Being practical and realistic
Following their parents
questions.why: He says it's 'more about pragmatism than it is about idealism'.

questions.q: What does Sam add about people moving to the right?
options: It happens to everyone
It only happens in the UK
It means they change their politics completely
It doesn't apply to everyone, or mean a complete change
questions.why: She says it doesn't apply to everyone and doesn't mean they completely change their politics.
